cases.whole_expression_finding: The actual whole historical prayer preserves the ordered inherited-death/Passion/image argument underlying the target. The target takes da from an alternate apparatus reading but eidem from the main text: no single cited old witness is the target. The separate Palm Sunday witness establishes the complete conclusion wording, not Good Friday appointment or Omnes respondent. Cumulative ritual editing remains contrary evidence. The prepared whole-expression account accurately preserves those facts and the prior narrow qualified/moderate assessment; this is not an independent legal clearance.
cases.boundaries: The complete target includes literal conclusion, nonspoken Omnes respondent: at character320, and spoken Amen. No source heading or adjacent ritual prose included.

cases.whole_expression_finding: The entire historical mercy/protection/Christ/blood/paschal-mystery prayer follows the same syntax and sequence. The target removes nobis and changes the actual old short conclusion. Both abridgment and conventional closure selection can contribute authorship; the Monday-sixth-week witness and Palm Sunday conclusion do not prove Good Friday appointment or the whole modern expression public domain. Those qualifications remain explicit and are factually supported.
cases.boundaries: The preceding Oremus is outside this frozen body. R. at character208 is nonspoken; following Amen remains spoken. No inferred liturgical expansion.

cases.whole_expression_finding: The complete already-Marian Holy House Secret preserves offering acceptance, supporting merits, and saving result in the same order. Replacing the local setting and worthily-offered description with laetantis Ecclesiae and adding/reordering the royal Marian title are substantive redaction. Eufymia and Laurence are whole corroborating historical prayers, not a license to assemble an allegedly public-domain target from phrases. The prepared qualified whole-expression account preserves this distinction.
cases.boundaries: Exact unit2692 only; literal Per Dominum. retained. Running header on Mame[42] names the next Common; heading pages[40]–[41] establish this prayer belongs to Translation of the Holy House.

cases.whole_expression_finding: The complete Celebratis prayer preserves the sequence of completed rites, intercession, saving result, and joyful observance. The target adds solemniis, substitutes the honoree/feast including memoria, changes plural pronouns and honor language, moves fiant, and replaces per. with actual Per Dominum. Those substantive modern choices remain contrary evidence; the record does not claim a generic title-swap rule or whole-target historical identity.
cases.boundaries: Exact unit2695 includes parenthetical memoria and short Per Dominum. Actual historical prayer is printed39 VIII Celebratis ... impleta, not printed41 XII Peractis ... impensa.
cases.nonblocking_observation: Candidate source locator lines27–30 includes one preceding prayer line. Exact Celebratis prayer occupies28–30. Incipit, whole-prayer payload, and physical-line1 selection are correct; tighten locator wording when convenient without changing frozen body.

cases.whole_expression_finding: The historical collect preserves the connected Church/foundation/gates/steadfastness framework. The source units do not supply the whole target: apostolicae petrae, named Summo Pontifice intercession in this position, virtute persistens assembled from different older readings, and continua securitate muniatur remain modern choices. The whole preface says virtute consistens; the old collect says veritate persistens. The protection prayer supplies a relation rather than the new ending. These are substantial contrary facts, accurately retained as the strongest originality objection in the narrow qualified/moderate account.
cases.boundaries: Own Urban Collect2639 with virtute is retained. Common veritate is not substituted. Literal Per Dominum. remains unexpanded.

cases.whole_expression_finding: The complete old antiphon preserves the same ordered construction apart from dicent to dicunt and pointing/case/quotation marks. Dicent is future and dicunt present; this is a real tense change, not spelling. The qualified account treats that change in the context of the whole expression and does not use shortness, phrase availability, or a similarity ratio as blanket clearance.
